body:
NX8's 8-bit static formats lose most on linear outputs: PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors keeps only -19.0 dB SQNR (signal-to-quantization-noise ratio; higher is better) there even in its best format (fp8_e3m4). Measured on 36 models with a format search (of 665 surveyed).

Model outputs keep a median 22.1 dB SQNR against full precision, the worst -2.4 dB (Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B). 16 of 31 models with a labelled metric lose some of it; the most: jonatasgrosman/wav2vec2-large-xlsr-53-japanese (agreement -1), openai/whisper-base (agreement -1) and openai/whisper-large-v3-turbo (agreement -1).

The tensors that lose most even in their best format: linear in PaddlePaddle/PP-DocLayoutV3_safetensors (fp8_e3m4, -19.0 dB), bmm in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -16.1 dB), bmm in openai/whisper-small (fp8_e3m4, -15.0 dB), mul in openai/whisper-small (fp8_e3m4, -15.0 dB), sin in microsoft/table-transformer-structure-recognition (fp8_e3m4, -14.4 dB), bmm in Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (fp8_e2m5, -14.0 dB), linear in Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (fp8_e3m4, -13.6 dB), linear in EleutherAI/pythia-160m (fp8_e3m4, -12.1 dB), linear in Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (fp8_e2m5, -12.0 dB) and linear in Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (fp8_e3m4, -11.5 dB).

Formats chosen (E = exponent bits, M = mantissa bits, u = unsigned): fp8_e2m5 10995 (45%), fp8_e3m4 10063 (42%), fp8_e1m6 2775 (11%), ufp8_e2m6 264 (1.09%), ufp8_e1m7 125 (0.52%), ufp8_e3m5 22 (0.09%), fp8_e4m3 1 (under 0.01%); 1.70% of tensors use an unsigned format.

A wider format or a per-row choice would recover most where the most data carries the most error: linear in Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (fp8_e2m5, -2.4 dB), linear in Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (fp8_e3m4, 0.3 dB) and linear in Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (fp8_e3m4, 1.0 dB).

7 missing capabilities keep 65 operations in 14 models (of 26 planned) off the chip's direct path; the most widespread is run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip) (45 operations in 9 models). Ranked by the MACs they hold:

**Lowering a convolution padded by name.** The planner does not lower a conv2d whose padding is given by name ('valid') rather than by size, so it needs a workaround; this is a gap of the lowering, not of the ISA. It affects 1 operation in 1 model: 1 call (0.01% of all calls) and 116 M MACs (under 0.01% of all MACs); the biggest: conv2d in prithivMLmods/Gender-Classifier-Mini. Cost today: 0 of 1 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 1 wait for one; 4 workarounds proposed, 0 passing its check, none evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**Run-time addressing (a load from an address computed on chip).** The chip cannot read memory at an address computed at run time, so every lookup or choice by a run-time value (embedding and gather) needs a workaround. It affects 45 operations in 9 models: 45 calls (0.55% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: embedding in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256, embedding in BAAI/bge-reranker-large and embedding in SamLowe/roberta-base-go_emotions. Cost today: 0 of 45 have a workaround (0 exact, 0 approximate), 0 failed and 45 wait for one; 77 workarounds proposed, 29 passing its check, 13 evaluated on a model; accuracy not measured yet; cycles not measured yet; 0 extra kernels.

**An upsample instruction.** The chip has no instruction for upsample, so every upsample needs a workaround. It affects 11 operations in 3 models: 11 calls (0.13% of all calls) and no MACs (data movement only); the biggest: upsample in mattmdjaga/segformer_b2_clothes, upsample in nvidia/segformer-b2-finetuned-ade-512-512 and upsample in nvidia/segformer-b0-finetuned-ade-512-512. **A cumsum instruction.** The chip has no instruction for cumsum, so every cumsum needs a workaround. title: Missing instructions: 65 operations in 14 models need workarounds

body:
A kernel reads a tensor in the arrangement its writer stored it in; when the reader needs another arrangement, the reading kernel has to rearrange the data itself. This happens to 680 of 1467 tensors passed between kernels (46%) in 22 models: 416 for attention heads split or merged, 238 for other reshapes, 17 for pixels reordered, 6 for dimensions merged and 3 for image patches.

The reading operations are 519 operations (519 calls, 6.37% of all calls; 118 G MACs, 4.02% of all MACs). The most common causes (writer → reader): linear → attention (attention heads split or merged) 207, linear → bmm (attention heads split or merged) 128 and linear → add (other reshapes) 58; most in facebook/DiT-XL-2-256 (196), Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B (137) and stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5 (129).

Cost today: extra cycles not measured yet (no reading kernel has run); 0 links fail.
title: Layout conversions: 680 of 1467 tensors between kernels are rearranged

body:
Activations such as exp, GELU and reciprocal go through a 256-entry lookup table (LUT), which limits their precision: 2,019 operations in 24 models (2,019 calls, 25% of all calls), most often layernorm (604), silu (340) and softmax (277). Their quantized accuracy: worst -3.5 dB SQNR over 1,235 measured operations.

Kernels per forward pass (host launches, one per planned kernel call): median 11, most 65 (stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5, 65 planned groups), over 26 models.

FP32 headroom (how far the largest value is from FP32 overflow, in powers of ten) is least at 33.1 powers of ten for bmm in Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (largest value 2.75e+05).

181 outputs in 11 models hold a value at the FP32 limit itself (mostly add (165), select_where (13) and amin (2), e.g. an attention mask's fill value); they are counted apart from the headroom.

Instruction memory (IMEM, 1,024 words per bank) use: not measured yet (no kernel built).
title: Resource limits: 2,019 operations limited by the LUT and up to 65 kernel launches per pass

body: The costliest measured cost is **quantization accuracy**: NX8's 8-bit static formats lose a median 22.1 dB SQNR against full precision (worst −3.0 dB on Qwen3-0.6B), with linear outputs hit hardest (worst −19.0 dB in PP-DocLayoutV3), and 16 of 31 labelled models lose some end-metric accuracy. Next is **resource limits**: 1,748 operations (26% of calls) go through a 256-entry LUT whose worst measured accuracy is 1.9 dB SQNR, and forward passes need a median 10.5 kernel launches (up to 65 for stable-diffusion-v1-5). Third is **layout conversions**: 47% of tensors passed between kernels (530 of 1,131) must be rearranged by the reading kernel, mostly for attention-head splits, touching 5.6% of calls and 4.0% of MACs — though the extra cycles are not yet measured. Fourth is **missing instructions**: 65 operations in 13 models need workarounds, dominated by run-time addressing (45 operations, 8 models), and only cumsum has a working workaround (losing 0.00 dB); the rest have none passing checks or none evaluated. Least costly is the **named-padding conv2d lowering gap**, affecting a single call and 0.01% of MACs. Across all categories, cycles, MAC utilisation and IMEM use are still unmeasured, and no workaround has added extra kernels.
